items.stem: Define the term 'competition policy'.
items.answer: Government laws and regulators that promote competition and prevent abuse of market power, e.g. by investigating mergers, cartels and monopolies.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, government laws and regulators that promote competition and prevent abuse of market power, e.g. by investigating mergers, cartels and monopolies. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why governments use competition policy.
items.answer: To stop firms abusing market power by charging high prices, restricting choice or blocking new entrants, so consumers get lower prices, more choice and more innovation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark prevent abuse of market power; 1 mark benefit to consumers (price/choice/innovation). [2]

items.stem: Explain one benefit and one cost to a business of stricter government regulation of its industry.
items.answer: Benefit: rules create a level playing field and can raise consumer trust; cost: compliance costs (staff, reporting, equipment) raise unit costs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark benefit + explanation; 1 mark cost + explanation. [2]

items.stem: Based in Kuala Lumpur, BatikPay Sdn Bhd (private limited company) runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops. The business has around 210 employees. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. Explain how a decision by the competition authority to investigate BatikPay's pricing could affect the business.
items.answer: Points to develop for BatikPay: competition law prevents abuse of a dominant position; possible fines and legal costs; damage to reputation with customers and investors; may have to change pricing or contracts, reducing profit.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: competition law prevents abuse of a dominant position. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (BatikPay: financial technology, about 210 employees, private limited company in Malaysia; the central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for BatikPay, e.g. possible fines and legal costs; damage to reputation with customers and investors; may have to change pricing or contracts, reducing profit. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Indus Sports Goods Ltd is a private limited company based in Karachi, Pakistan. It makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment and employs about 950 people. A rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices. Explain two ways in which new government regulations on product safety could affect Indus Sports.
items.answer: Points to develop for Indus Sports: regulation sets legal minimum standards; higher costs of testing and redesigning footballs and cricket equipment; delays to new product launches; can become a source of competitive advantage if rivals struggle to comply.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: regulation sets legal minimum standards. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Indus Sports: sports equipment manufacturing, about 950 employees, private limited company in Pakistan; a rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Indus Sports, e.g. higher costs of testing and redesigning footballs and cricket equipment; delays to new product launches; can become a source of competitive advantage if rivals struggle to comply. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Lisbon, Tejo Mobility SA (public limited company) assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union. The business has around 600 employees. Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. Evaluate whether government regulation of its industry is more of a threat than an opportunity for Tejo Mobility.
items.answer: For: compliance costs and fines; restrictions on pricing and products; management time diverted. Against: raises barriers to entry for rivals; improves consumer trust; early compliance can be a selling point. Judgement: the decision for Tejo Mobility depends mainly on how strict and how well enforced the rules are, and also on its size relative to competitors.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Tejo Mobility: vehicle manufacturing, about 600 employees, public limited company in Portugal; battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. compliance costs and fines; restrictions on pricing and products; management time diverted; arguments against, e.g. raises barriers to entry for rivals; improves consumer trust; early compliance can be a selling point. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how strict and how well enforced the rules are; its size relative to competitors; whether it can pass costs on. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Tejo Mobility, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Muscat Dates & Co. LLC is a family-owned limited company based in Muscat, Oman. It processes, packs and exports dates and date syrup and employs about 160 people. Three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor. Explain one advantage to Muscat Dates of stricter government regulation of its industry.
items.answer: Protects reputation of compliant firms.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. protects reputation of compliant firms; barriers to entry deter new rivals; consumer confidence in packed dates and date syrup may rise. 1 mark: explained in the context of Muscat Dates (food processing). [2]

items.stem: Explain how deregulation of a market might affect an existing firm in that market.
items.answer: New competitors can enter, so prices and market share may fall; but the firm also gains freedom to enter new activities and may become more efficient.
items.markingKey: 1 mark more competition / lower prices; 1 mark new freedoms or efficiency pressure. [2]

items.stem: Annual sales in a market are: Cape Brew $130m, Lanka Tea $85m, Savanna Fresh $70m, Nile Pharma $65m, Gold Coast Cocoa $40m; all other firms $120m. Calculate the three-firm concentration ratio.

Annual sales in a market are: IslaConnect $135m, Muscat Dates $105m, Desert Bloom $85m, Bosphorus Home $40m, BatikPay $35m; all other firms $260m. Calculate the three-firm concentration ratio. Bosphorus Home and BatikPay propose to merge. Calculate their combined market share.
items.answer: CR3 = 49.2%; combined share 11.4%

items.stem: Define the term 'minimum wage'.
items.answer: The lowest hourly rate of pay that an employer is legally allowed to pay a worker.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the lowest hourly rate of pay that an employer is legally allowed to pay a worker. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one reason why governments pass consumer protection laws.
items.answer: Consumers often have less information than producers, so laws prevent unsafe or misleadingly described products and give buyers a remedy if goods are faulty.
items.markingKey: 1 mark reason (information gap/safety/unfair practices); 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a large rise in the minimum wage could affect a labour-intensive business.
items.answer: Wage costs and unit costs rise, cutting margins unless prices rise; it may substitute capital for labour or reduce hours, but motivation and retention may improve.
items.markingKey: 1 mark higher costs; 1 mark response (prices/automation); 1 mark possible benefit. [3]

items.stem: Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. IslaConnect Inc., a private limited company in the Philippines with about 2,600 employees, runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia. Explain how stricter employment laws on working hours could affect IslaConnect.
items.answer: Points to develop for IslaConnect: employment law sets maximum hours and rest periods; more staff may be needed to cover the same work, raising costs; less fatigue may improve productivity and safety; scheduling and flexibility become more difficult.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: employment law sets maximum hours and rest periods. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (IslaConnect: business process outsourcing, about 2,600 employees, private limited company in the Philippines; clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for IslaConnect, e.g. more staff may be needed to cover the same work, raising costs; less fatigue may improve productivity and safety; scheduling and flexibility become more difficult. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Maple Learning Inc., a private limited company in Canada with about 260 employees, runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students. Explain the possible effects on Maple Learning of a large increase in the minimum wage.
items.answer: Points to develop for Maple Learning: minimum wage is a legal floor on hourly pay; labour costs rise in proportion to the number of low-paid staff; may raise prices or automate to protect margins; motivation and retention may improve.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: minimum wage is a legal floor on hourly pay. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Maple Learning: education technology, about 260 employees, private limited company in Canada; venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Maple Learning, e.g. labour costs rise in proportion to the number of low-paid staff; may raise prices or automate to protect margins; motivation and retention may improve. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Kiwi Trails Ltd is a private limited company based in Auckland, New Zealand. It runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours and employs about 90 people. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Evaluate the impact of a large rise in the minimum wage on Kiwi Trails.
items.answer: For: higher labour costs and lower margins; need to raise prices; differentials with supervisors narrow. Against: better motivation and lower turnover; customers may have more to spend; rivals face the same cost increase. Judgement: the decision for Kiwi Trails depends mainly on how labour-intensive its operations are, and also on the price elasticity of demand for its adventure tours.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Kiwi Trails: tourism, about 90 employees, private limited company in New Zealand; bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. higher labour costs and lower margins; need to raise prices; differentials with supervisors narrow; arguments against, e.g. better motivation and lower turnover; customers may have more to spend; rivals face the same cost increase. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how labour-intensive its operations are; the price elasticity of demand for its adventure tours; how many of its staff are on the minimum wage. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Kiwi Trails, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Explain one advantage to Pearl Logistics of new laws giving consumers longer guarantees on freight and warehousing services.
items.answer: Customer trust and repeat purchases may rise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. customer trust and repeat purchases may rise; quality becomes a selling point; weaker rivals may leave the market. 1 mark: explained in the context of Pearl Logistics (logistics). [2]

items.stem: The minimum wage of $9 per hour rises by 12%. What is the new minimum wage?

IslaConnect Inc. employs 400 workers on the minimum wage, each working 40 hours a week for 52 weeks a year. The minimum wage rises by 5% from $12 per hour. Calculate the increase in the annual wage bill for these workers.

Indus Sports Goods Ltd is a private limited company based in Karachi, Pakistan. It makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment and employs about 950 people. A rival in China has started selling machine-made balls at lower prices. (a) Define 'unfair dismissal'. (b) Explain one advantage to Indus Sports of a 12% rise in the national minimum wage in Pakistan.
items.answer: (a) Ending an employee's contract without a fair reason (such as misconduct, incapability or genuine redundancy) or without following a fair procedure. (b) Low-paid staff may be more motivated.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (low-paid staff may be more motivated; labour turnover and recruitment costs may fall; customers on low incomes have more to spend on footballs and cricket equipment), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Indus Sports [3]

It brews craft beers and low-sugar soft drinks sold through bars and supermarkets and employs about 140 people. Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Using the case and your own knowledge, evaluate the impact of a large rise in the minimum wage on Cape Brew.
items.answer: For: higher labour costs and lower margins; need to raise prices; differentials with supervisors narrow. Against: better motivation and lower turnover; customers may have more to spend; rivals face the same cost increase. Judgement: the decision for Cape Brew depends mainly on how labour-intensive its operations are, and also on the price elasticity of demand for its craft beer and soft drinks.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Cape Brew: beverages, about 140 employees, private limited company in South Africa; demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce). AO3 Analysis [5]: arguments for, e.g. higher labour costs and lower margins; need to raise prices; differentials with supervisors narrow; arguments against, e.g. better motivation and lower turnover; customers may have more to spend; rivals face the same cost increase. AO4 Evaluation [5]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how labour-intensive its operations are; the price elasticity of demand for its craft beer and soft drinks; how many of its staff are on the minimum wage. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Cape Brew, not a generic one. [16]

items.stem: Define the term 'corporate social responsibility (CSR)'.
items.answer: The idea that a business should take account of the interests of all its stakeholders and society, not just its shareholders, when making decisions.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the idea that a business should take account of the interests of all its stakeholders and society, not just its shareholders, when making decisions. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why accepting corporate social responsibility might increase a firm's long-term profits.
items.answer: A responsible image attracts customers and staff, reduces the risk of boycotts and fines, and can lower costs (e.g. less waste), raising long-run profit even if short-run costs rise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark reputation/demand; 1 mark recruitment/retention or reduced risk; 1 mark short-run cost v long-run gain. [3]

items.stem: Explain one way an ageing population could affect a business's workforce planning.
items.answer: More employees retire and fewer young people join, so the business may face skills shortages and need to retain older workers, retrain staff or recruit migrants.
items.markingKey: 1 mark effect on labour supply; 1 mark planning response. [2]

items.stem: The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Andina Solar SpA, a private limited company in Chile with about 380 employees, designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes. Explain how changes in the age structure of the population of Chile could affect Andina Solar.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andina Solar: demographic change alters the size and needs of market segments; demand for solar installations may rise or fall in different age groups; labour shortages if fewer young workers; need to adapt marketing mix and recruitment.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: demographic change alters the size and needs of market segments. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Andina Solar: renewable energy, about 380 employees, private limited company in Chile; the government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Andina Solar, e.g. demand for solar installations may rise or fall in different age groups; labour shortages if fewer young workers; need to adapt marketing mix and recruitment. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research. Lumen Robotics plc, a public limited company in Singapore with about 2,400 employees, designs and builds robots used on factory assembly lines. Explain how Lumen Robotics could benefit from publishing a social audit.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lumen Robotics: a social audit reports social and environmental impact; transparency builds trust with customers and investors; identifies areas to improve and cut waste; may attract ethical investors and staff.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a social audit reports social and environmental impact. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Lumen Robotics: industrial engineering, about 2,400 employees, public limited company in Singapore; shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Lumen Robotics, e.g. transparency builds trust with customers and investors; identifies areas to improve and cut waste; may attract ethical investors and staff. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Muscat, Muscat Dates & Co. LLC (family-owned limited company) processes, packs and exports dates and date syrup. The business has around 160 employees. Three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor. Discuss the extent to which social and demographic change is the most important external influence on Muscat Dates.
items.answer: For: changes the size of its market segments; affects labour supply and skills; shifts consumer tastes. Against: economic factors such as incomes may matter more; technology and competition may be more urgent; demographic change is slow and predictable. Judgement: the decision for Muscat Dates depends mainly on the time horizon being considered, and also on the products it sells.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Muscat Dates: food processing, about 160 employees, family-owned limited company in Oman; three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. changes the size of its market segments; affects labour supply and skills; shifts consumer tastes; arguments against, e.g. economic factors such as incomes may matter more; technology and competition may be more urgent; demographic change is slow and predictable. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the time horizon being considered; the products it sells; how quickly it can adapt. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Muscat Dates, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which demographic change is most likely to increase demand for healthcare products?
options: Emigration of older people
Falling life expectancy
An ageing population
A rising birth rate
items.answer: An ageing population
items.markingKey: An ageing population. More older people increase demand for medicines, care and health services.

items.stem: Explain why the interests of shareholders and the local community may conflict.
items.answer: Shareholders want higher profit and dividends, which may mean cutting costs or relocating; the community wants jobs, a clean environment and support for local projects.
items.markingKey: 1 mark shareholder objective; 1 mark community objective and conflict. [2]

Mekong Furniture JSC, a joint stock company in Vietnam with about 1,200 employees, makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe. Explain how Mekong Furniture could benefit from publishing a social audit.
items.answer: Points to develop for Mekong Furniture: a social audit reports social and environmental impact; transparency builds trust with customers and investors; identifies areas to improve and cut waste; may attract ethical investors and staff.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a social audit reports social and environmental impact. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Mekong Furniture: furniture manufacturing, about 1,200 employees, joint stock company in Vietnam; a major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Mekong Furniture, e.g. transparency builds trust with customers and investors; identifies areas to improve and cut waste; may attract ethical investors and staff. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd, a private limited company in Ghana with about 450 employees, buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. Explain how Gold Coast Cocoa could benefit from publishing a social audit.
items.answer: Points to develop for Gold Coast Cocoa: a social audit reports social and environmental impact; transparency builds trust with customers and investors; identifies areas to improve and cut waste; may attract ethical investors and staff.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a social audit reports social and environmental impact. items.stem: Based in Cairo, Nile Pharma plc (public limited company) manufactures generic medicines for hospitals and pharmacies in Africa and the Middle East. The business has around 1,800 employees. Most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars. (a) Define 'corporate social responsibility (CSR)'. (b) Explain one advantage to Nile Pharma of adopting a strong corporate social responsibility policy.
items.answer: (a) The idea that a business should take account of the interests of all its stakeholders and society, not just its shareholders, when making decisions. (b) Better brand image and customer loyalty.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (better brand image and customer loyalty; easier to recruit and keep staff; reduced risk of legal action or boycotts), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Nile Pharma [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'technological change'.
items.answer: The development of new products, processes and ways of working through advances in knowledge, e.g. automation, artificial intelligence and e-commerce.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the development of new products, processes and ways of working through advances in knowledge, e.g. automation, artificial intelligence and e-commerce. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Which is most likely to be a benefit to a business of introducing new technology?
options: Immediate rise in employee morale
Lower initial capital cost
Lower unit costs through higher labour productivity
No need to train staff
items.answer: Lower unit costs through higher labour productivity
items.markingKey: Lower unit costs through higher labour productivity. Technology often raises productivity but needs investment and training.

items.stem: Explain why some employees resist the introduction of new technology.
items.answer: They may fear job losses, loss of skills or status, and the stress of learning new methods; changes to routines create uncertainty.
items.markingKey: 1 mark fear of redundancy/deskilling; 1 mark uncertainty/retraining. [2]

LLC, a family-owned limited company in Oman with about 160 employees, processes, packs and exports dates and date syrup. items.answer: Points to develop for Muscat Dates: technological change creates new products and processes; opportunity to cut costs and improve quality; risk that existing packed dates and date syrup become obsolete; investment and retraining needed to keep up.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: technological change creates new products and processes. items.answer: For: lower unit costs; higher quality and speed; keeps up with competitors. items.stem: Explain how reducing its environmental impact could lower a business's costs.
items.answer: Using less energy and materials, recycling waste and avoiding fines or carbon taxes all cut costs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark method; 1 mark link to cost saving. [2]

items.stem: Inflation in Turkey has been above 40% for two years. Explain how pressure from customers and governments to reduce environmental damage could affect Bosphorus Home, and judge which point is most important for Bosphorus Home.
items.answer: Points to develop for Bosphorus Home: environmental pressure from stakeholders and regulation; higher costs of cleaner processes and materials; opportunity to differentiate household appliances as sustainable; risk of reputational damage if it fails to act.

items.stem: Which action is most likely to be investigated by a competition authority?
options: A firm cutting its costs through new technology
A firm advertising its products on social media
Two leading firms agreeing to charge the same price
A small firm entering a new market
items.answer: Two leading firms agreeing to charge the same price
items.markingKey: Two leading firms agreeing to charge the same price. Price fixing is collusion between rivals and is illegal under competition law.
